to civil proceedings for loss, damage or injury of any kind suffered by another person because of that conduct; or
to disciplinary action, or to a disciplinary sanction, of any kind because of that conduct.

section.heading: Disclosing OBR information, CVR information, and restricted information given by the ATSB, where serious offence imminent

content.p: The Inspector may apply to an eligible Judge or nominated ART member for an order under subsection (6) allowing the Inspector to disclose OBR information, CVR information, or restricted information given to the Inspector by the ATSB, to another government agency, if the Inspector suspects on reasonable grounds that:
the commission of an offence is imminent; and
the offence is an offence against a law of the Commonwealth, or of a State or Territory, punishable by a maximum penalty of imprisonment for more than 2 years; and
the information may be relevant to the prevention of the offence.
The application may be made in writing or, if the Inspector thinks it is necessary because of urgent circumstances, by telephone.
The application must be accompanied by:
a statement by the Inspector, or a delegate of the Inspector, of his or her grounds for suspecting that an offence of the kind mentioned in paragraph (1)(b) is imminent; and
a statement by the Inspector, or a delegate of the Inspector, explaining why the information may be relevant to the prevention of the offence; and

(c) a statement by the Chief Commissioner of the ATSB, or a delegate of the Chief Commissioner, that, in his or her opinion, the effect that the disclosure may have on current or future investigations under the Transport Safety Investigation Act 2003 is outweighed by the public interest served by disclosing the information to the agency or court; and
the proposed terms of the order.
If the application is made in writing, the accompanying statements and the proposed terms of the order must be in writing.
If the application is made by telephone:

the accompanying statements may be given by telephone, provided the person making the statement gives the Judge or ART member to whom the statement is made, on the next day after the statement is made that is not a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in the place where it is made, an affidavit containing:
a copy of the statement made to the Judge or ART member by telephone; and
a statement that the copy is a true record of the statement made to the Judge or ART member by telephone; and
the proposed terms of the order must be communicated to the Judge or ART member by telephone; and
the Inspector must inform the Judge or ART member to whom the application is made of the urgent circumstances on the basis of which the Inspector believes a telephone application is necessary.
An eligible Judge or nominated ART member may order that OBR information, CVR information, or restricted information given to the Inspector by the ATSB, be disclosed to a government agency if:
the Judge or ART member is satisfied that:
an offence of the kind mentioned in paragraph (1)(b) is imminent; and
the information may be relevant to the prevention of the offence; and
having regard to the following matters, it is appropriate to make the order:
the extent to which the privacy of any person may be affected by the disclosure;
the seriousness of the offence;
the likelihood that the disclosure of the information would assist the agency in the prevention of the offence;
the likelihood that the offence would be prevented without the disclosure of the information to the agency;
(v) the effect that the disclosure may have on current or future investigations under the Transport Safety Investigation Act 2003.
The order may include conditions or restrictions on the disclosure of the information.
If the application for the order was made by telephone, the Judge or ART member must, as soon as practicable after making the order:
inform the Inspector or, if the application was made by a delegate of the Inspector, the delegate, of:
the terms of the order; and
the day on which it was made; and
the time at which it was made; and
give the order to the Inspector or delegate.

The government agency to which information is disclosed on the order of the Judge or ART member must not copy, make a record of, use or disclose the information for any purpose that is not related to the prevention of an offence against a law of the Commonwealth, or of a State or Territory, punishable by a maximum penalty of imprisonment for more than 2 years.
The Judge or ART member may copy, make a record of, use or disclose any information given to the Judge or ART member under this section for the purposes of exercising the powers under this section.

A person assisting the Judge or ART member in the exercise of powers under this section may copy, make a record of, use or disclose information given to that person in the course of providing that assistance, but only for the purpose of providing that assistance.
In this Act:
eligible Judge means a Judge in relation to whom a consent under subsection (2) and a declaration under subsection (3) are in force.
Judge means a person who is a Judge of a court created by the Parliament.
A Judge may, by writing, consent to be nominated by the Attorney-General under subsection (3).
The Attorney-General may, by writing, declare Judges in relation to whom consents are in force under subsection (2) to be eligible Judges for the purposes of this Act.

An eligible Judge has, in relation to the performance or exercise of a function or power conferred on an eligible Judge by this Act, the same protection and immunity as a Justice of the High Court has in relation to proceedings in the High Court.
Any function or power conferred on an eligible Judge under this Act is so conferred only in a personal capacity and not as a court or a member of a court.
The Attorney-General may, by writing, nominate a person who holds one of the following appointments to the Administrative Review Tribunal to make orders under subsection 77(6):
President;
Deputy President;
senior member.
Despite subsection (1), the Attorney-General must not nominate a person who holds an appointment as a senior member unless the person:
is enrolled as a legal practitioner of the High Court, of another federal court or of the Supreme Court of a State or of the Northern Territory or the Australian Capital Territory; and
has been so enrolled for not less than 5 years.
A nomination ceases to have effect if:
the nominated ART member ceases to hold an appointment of a kind set out in subsection (1); or
the Attorney-General, by writing, withdraws the nomination.

A nominated ART member has, in relation to the performance or exercise of a function or power conferred on a nominated ART member by this Act, the same protection and immunity as a Justice of the High Court has in relation to proceedings in the High Court.

section.heading: Inspector to minimise disruption to transport

content.p: In exercising powers and performing functions under this Act, the Inspector must have regard to the desirability of minimising any resulting disruption to:
transport by means of transport vehicles; and
the operation of security regulated offshore facilities.

section.heading: Inspector to act consistently with Australia’s international obligations

content.p: The Inspector, and each delegate of the Inspector, must exercise the Inspector’s powers and perform the Inspector’s functions under this Act in a manner that is consistent with Australia’s obligations under international agreements (as in force from time to time) that are identified by the regulations for the purposes of this section.
The Inspector may, by writing, delegate all or any of the Inspector’s powers and functions to:
an SES employee; or
a person who holds or performs the duties of an APS Executive Level 1 or 2 position or an equivalent position; or
a person who:
is engaged by the Commonwealth, under contract or otherwise, to exercise powers, or perform functions, of the Inspector under this Act; and
satisfies the criteria prescribed by the regulations.
The ATSB may, by writing, delegate all or any of the ATSB’s powers and functions under this Act to:
an SES employee; or
a person who holds or performs the duties of an APS Executive Level 1 or 2 position or an equivalent position.
The Chief Commissioner of the ATSB may, by writing, delegate all or any of his or her powers and functions under this Act to:
an SES employee; or
a person who holds or performs the duties of an APS Executive Level 1 or 2 position or an equivalent position.

section.heading: States and Territories may confer powers and functions on Inspector

content.p: A law of a State or Territory may confer powers and functions on the Inspector.
In enacting subsection (1), it is the intention of the Parliament to rely on all powers available to it under the Constitution.
To the extent that the Inspector has a power or function that is conferred, or taken to be conferred, by the law of a State or Territory:
that power or function is not taken to be conferred by Commonwealth law; and
subsection (1) is not taken to authorise the conferral of the power or function;

if the conferral or authorisation would contravene a constitutional doctrine restricting the powers and functions that may be conferred on authorities or officers of the Commonwealth, or would otherwise exceed the legislative power of the Commonwealth.

If, to ensure the validity of the conferral of a power or function purportedly conferred on the Inspector by a law of a State or Territory, it is necessary that the power or function be conferred by a law of the Commonwealth, rather than by a law of a State, the power or function is taken to be conferred by this Act to the extent necessary to ensure that validity.

If, because of subsection (4), this Act is taken to confer a power or function upon the Inspector, it is the intention of the Parliament to rely on all powers available to it under the Constitution to support the conferral of the power or function.
Subsections (4) and (5) do not limit subsection (1).

section.heading: Immunity for actions under this Act

content.p: This section does not apply to the copying, recording use or disclosure of protected information, OBR information, CVR information, or restricted information.
This section applies where a person acts:
in the exercise of a power, or the performance of a function under this Act; or
in the honest and reasonable belief that the person is exercising a power, or performing a function under this Act; or
as otherwise permitted, either expressly or by implication, under this Act; or
in the honest and reasonable belief that he or she is acting as otherwise permitted, either expressly or by implication, under this Act.
The person is not liable:
to any proceedings for contravening any other law because of that conduct; or
to civil proceedings for loss, damage or injury of any kind suffered by another person because of that conduct; or
to disciplinary action, or to a disciplinary sanction, of any kind because of that conduct.
This section applies in the following circumstances:
the Minister fails to take action in the course of doing any thing:
in the exercise of a power, or the performance of a function under this Act; or
in the honest and reasonable belief that the Minister is exercising a power, or performing a function under this Act; or
permitted, either expressly or by implication, to be done under this Act; or
that the Minister honestly and reasonably believes is permitted, either expressly or by implication, to be done under this Act;
the Inspector fails to take action in the course of doing any thing:
in the exercise of a power, or the performance of a function under this Act; or
in the honest and reasonable belief that the Inspector is exercising a power, or performing a function under this Act; or
permitted, either expressly or by implication, to be done under this Act; or
that the Inspector honestly and reasonably believes is permitted, either expressly or by implication, to be done under this Act;
a person fails to take action in the course of doing any thing:
permitted to be done under a delegation under section 82; or
that the person honestly and reasonably believes is permitted to be done under a delegation under section 82.
Neither the Minister, the Inspector nor the person is liable:
to any proceedings for contravening any other law because of that conduct; or
to civil proceedings for loss, damage or injury of any kind suffered by another person because of that conduct.

section.heading: Certification by Inspector of a person’s involvement in an inquiry

content.p: The Inspector may issue a certificate stating that a specified person:
is exercising or has exercised powers under this Act in relation to a specified matter; or
is performing or has performed functions under this Act in relation to a specified matter; or
is assisting or has assisted another person in the exercise of powers or the performance of functions under this Act in relation to a specified matter.
A person is not obliged to comply with a subpoena or similar direction of a court or tribunal to attend and answer questions relating to a matter if:
the person:
is exercising or has exercised powers under this Act in relation to the matter; or
is performing or has performed functions in relation to the matter; or
is assisting or has assisted another person in the exercise of powers or the performance of functions under this Act in relation to the matter; and
the Inspector has issued a certificate under section 86 for the person in relation to the matter.
This section does not apply to a coronial inquiry.
This section has effect despite any other law.

section.heading: Fees for attendance at coronial inquiries

content.p: If:
a person:
is exercising or has exercised powers under this Act in relation to the matter; or
is performing or has performed functions under this Act in relation to the matter; or
is assisting or has assisted another person in the exercise of powers or the performance of functions under this Act in relation to the matter; and
the person appears as a witness in a coronial inquiry; and
the person is asked to give an expert opinion; and
the Inspector has issued a certificate under section 86 in relation to the matter that is being investigated at the coronial inquiry;
then the State or Territory concerned is liable to pay a fee to the Commonwealth in respect of the expenses of that attendance.
The amount of the fee, and the due date for payment, are to be determined under the regulations.
If the fee remains unpaid, then it can be recovered by the Commonwealth as a debt in a court of competent jurisdiction.
If a person appears as a witness in a coronial inquiry and:
the person is asked to give an expert opinion; or
the Inspector has issued a certificate under section 86 for the person in relation to a matter that is being investigated at the coronial inquiry;
then the person is entitled to legal representation in respect of that appearance.
This section does not, by implication, affect any entitlement to legal representation that a person has in circumstances not covered by subsection (1).

section.heading: Operation of section 503A of the Migration Act 1958 not affected

content.p: Nothing in this Act affects the operation of section 503A of the Migration Act 1958.

section.heading: Powers of Parliament and Royal Commissions not affected

content.p: Nothing in this Act affects the information-gathering powers of:
the Parliament or a House of the Parliament; or
a Royal Commission.

If the operation of this Act would result in an acquisition of property from a person otherwise than on just terms, the Commonwealth is liable to pay a reasonable amount of compensation to the person.

If the Commonwealth and the person do not agree on the amount of the compensation, the person may institute proceedings in a court of competent jurisdiction for the recovery from the Commonwealth of such reasonable amount of compensation as the court determines.
In this section:
acquisition of property has the same meaning as in paragraph 51(xxxi) of the Constitution.
just terms has the same meaning as in paragraph 51(xxxi) of the Constitution.
The Governor-General may make regulations prescribing matters:
required or permitted by this Act to be prescribed; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act.
